quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quondam: quondam (adv.) — once, formerly, at one time
refert: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back; to reply, utter (3rd sg. pres.)
reges: rēx, rēgis (m.) — king (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (qui reges)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also rēgia, -ae (f.), palace, royal house (nom. sg.: rēgia Pīcī)
regnum: rēgnum, -ī (n.) — kingdom, realm; royal power, rule (nom./acc. sg.)
remordet: remordeō, remordēre — to gnaw back; to torment, trouble (3rd sg. pres.)
reppulit: repellō, -ere, reppulī, repulsum — to drive back, repel, spurn (3rd sg. perf.)
requirit: requīrō, -ere, -sīvī, -sītum — to ask after, seek, inquire into (3rd sg. pres.)
rere: reor, rērī, ratus sum — to think, reckon, suppose (2nd sg. pres., = rēris; deponent)
respice: respiciō, -ere, -spexī, -spectum — to look back at, look to (sg. imper.)
rumpit: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst; break silence with (3rd sg. pres.)
sacrum: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy (n. acc. sg.) · also m. acc. sg. (sacrum Polyphoetēn)
saevit: saeviō, -īre, -iī, -ītum — to rage, be fierce, storm (3rd sg. pres.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
sanguineam: sanguineus, -a, -um — bloody, blood-red, bloodshot (f. acc. sg.)
satis: satis (indecl. n., adv.) — enough, sufficient; adv., sufficiently
saturnia: Sāturnius, -a, -um — of Saturn; Sāturnia, daughter of Saturn, Juno (f. nom. sg.)
scelerata: scelerātus, -a, -um — accursed, wicked, defiled by crime (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sceptra: scēptrum, -ī (n.) — sceptre; royal power (acc./nom. pl., often for sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sede: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, site (abl. sg.)
segnior: sēgnis, -e — slow, sluggish; sēgnior (compar.), more sluggish (m./f. nom. sg.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
siqua: sī + qua — if any, if in any way (indef. qua, f. nom. sg., with gloria)
situ: situs, -ūs (m.) — neglect, mould, decay, filth (abl. sg.; sitū)
solum: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, soil, land (acc./nom. sg.); also sōlus, alone (n. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (sōlus, alone: hoc sōlum nōmen)
solvite: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loose, release, put aside (2nd pl. imper.)
spatiis: spatium, -ī (n.) — space, track, round, course (abl./dat. pl.)
stupet: stupeō, -ēre, stupuī — to be stunned, amazed, dumbstruck (3rd sg. pres.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sumere: sūmō, -ere, sumpsī, sumptum — to take, take up (pres. inf.; poenās sūmere, to exact vengeance)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
supra: suprā (adv., prep. + acc.) — above, over, on top
taedas: taeda, -ae (f.) — pine torch; wedding torch, marriage rites (acc. pl.)
talem: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f. acc. sg.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tantos: tantus, -a, -um — so great, so much (m. acc. pl.)
tectisque: tectum, -ī (n.) — roof; house, hall (abl. pl.) + -que, and
tege: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, shield, conceal (2nd sg. imper.)
templa: templum, -ī (n.) — temple, sanctuary, sacred precinct (acc./nom. pl.)
thalamum: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, marriage chamber, bed (acc. sg.)
thybridis: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (gen. sg., Greek form)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totamque: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (f. acc. sg.) + -que, and
tristis: tristis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy (m./f. nom. sg.; acc. pl. in -is = -ēs)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tueri: tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum — to watch, guard, protect (pres. inf., deponent)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbo: turbō, -inis (m.) — whirlwind, storm, spinning blast (nom. sg.)
turnique: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Amata's favoured suitor for Lavinia (gen. sg.) + -que, and
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
vacua: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, deserted, unguarded (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
vapor: vapor, vapōris (m.) — steam, hot vapour, heat (nom. sg.)
veluti: velut, velutī (adv.) — just as, as when
venire: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (pres. inf.)
veri: vērus, -a, -um — true; vērum (n.), the truth (n. gen. sg., as noun)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vicissim: vicissim (adv.) — in turn, in succession, on the other hand
victa: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres.: Vīs … vidēre?)
visa: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
viscera: viscus, vīsceris (n.) — flesh; pl. viscera, entrails (acc. pl.)
vitta: vitta, -ae (f.) — fillet, headband, ribbon (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
vocavit: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. perf.)
vocibus: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice; word, utterance (abl./dat. pl.)
vociferans: vōciferor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to cry aloud, shout (pres. part., f. nom. sg.)
volitans: volitō, -āre — to flit, fly about (pres. part., f. nom. sg., with Fama)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
vultus: vultus, -ūs (m.) — face, features, countenance (acc. pl.; also nom. sg.)
